synthid: Cross-Year Person Linkage and Synthetic ID Assignment

synthid-package.Rd

Turns a stacked multi-year panel of Form 990 compensation records (the parsed output of titleclassifier and peopleparser) into a panel keyed by a stable per-person identifier. The pipeline is:

  1. build_id_string() / create_emp_ids() – a canonical, human-readable record string and a deterministic hash used as the per-record key.

  2. link_year_pairs() – generate candidate pairs blocked on organization, compare name components, score with a within-organization surname-frequency adjustment, and select one-to-one matches within each ordered year pair.

  3. resolve_clusters() – close the accepted links into connected components, split any cluster that would place two people from the same organization-year together, and stamp one stable EMP_ID per cluster.

  4. link_panel() – the end-to-end orchestrator over the three steps.

Reviewing a linkage

A separate triage layer audits the output of link_panel() and feeds the upstream name parser. It does not change any EMP_ID; it only surfaces records worth a second look.

  • flag_links() scores every multi-record person on cross-year name consistency and sorts each questionable cluster into one primary category (nickname/spelling, compound surname, field-order swap, a parser artifact, or the residual review). link_review_queue() returns just the review cases – the genuinely uncertain links.

  • parse_fail_log() scans records for recoverable parser defects (a honorific fused to the given name, credentials leaked into the surname, a stray initial glued to the surname) and emits one input -> wrong parse -> expected row each, usable directly as peopleparser regression fixtures. parse_fail_tokens() rolls that log up into the small list of candidate title/credential tokens to add upstream.

See dev/generate_link_review.R for the end-to-end review + handoff run.
